description: EXPORT-kind conformance corpus for @agledger/verify-core verifyAuditExport. Each vector is a REAL /audit-export document produced by the agledger-api engine, then tamper-transformed; pass/fail + canonical FailureCode are asserted by the corpus runner.

vectors.note: Clean 3-entry signed chain verified against out-of-band keys.
Entry 2 row chainPosition renumbered to 5 — monotonic position broken; after sort the gap surfaces at the position-3 entry.
Genesis entry carries a non-null previousHash — chain head removed.
Entry 2 previousHash no longer matches entry 1 payloadHash.
Stored payloadHash on entry 2 != sha256(coseSign1).
Entry 2 is missing the coseSign1 field.
Entry 2 coseSign1 is non-COSE bytes (hash re-stamped so decode is what fails).
Entry 2 has a valid signature but its signed -65537 chain claim (prevHash) disagrees with the chain — the visible columns were renumbered after signing.
Entry 2 signature byte flipped; envelope still decodes and the chain claim matches, so signature verification is what fails.
Entry 2 references signingKeyId=ghost-key with no key embedded or out of band.
exportFormatVersion 3.0 — precedes any chain walk.
canonicalization JCS (not RFC8949-CDE) — precedes any chain walk.
Zero entries — a chain with nothing to verify is never a silent pass.
Clean chain, but the caller requires a key id no entry uses — policy violation at the first entry.

Entry 2 re-signed with the attacker key (identical predicate, consistent kid+column swap) and embedded in signingPublicKeys. With no options it PASSES, documenting that embedded keys are trusted by default. The requireOutOfBandKeys vector below is the same fixture failing closed.

Same consistent-key-swap fixture under requireOutOfBandKeys: entry 2 attacker key is embedded-only, so it fails closed. The vault key is supplied out of band, so entries 1 and 3 pass; the policy break surfaces at position 2.

Entry 2 re-signed with the attacker key but the signature-covered kid still names the vault key; the row signingKeyId column points at the attacker key. The kid binding (engine signing_key_drift mirror) fails it with no options.
Entry 2 denormalised payload rewritten while coseSign1 carries the original predicate — binding-integrity failure caught before any content evaluation.

Entry 2 actorOwnerId rewritten to an owner the chain never signed, with nothing else touched — the action re-attributed to another actor after export. Must fail even under out-of-band keys, where every signature still verifies.

DRAFT-stage PATCH /v1/records/{id} edit: RECORD_CREATED then RECORD_UPDATED. verify-core projects RECORD_UPDATED through the generic record-state path; this vector pins the wire shape verifies green against out-of-band keys.

POST /v1/records with autoActivate: RECORD_CREATED signs status and state, then two RECORD_STATE_CHANGE entries sign previousStatus/newStatus beside previousState/newState. The DRAFT to REGISTERED hop reads CREATED to CREATED on the display pair, so only the internal pair says what moved.
Entry 2 row newState rewritten from REGISTERED to ACTIVE while the display pair still reads CREATED to CREATED. The internal state is in the signed payload, so the rewrite fails the payload binding.

POST /v1/records authenticated by an ephemeral cert, with X-Agent-Signature over the body hash. predicate.on_behalf_of seals the OIDC identity (validated: true), the cert {id, thumbprint, expires_at} and agent_signature {alg, content_hash, signature}. keys-agent.json is the publicKeyJwk signed into that cert's EPHEMERAL_CERT_ISSUED platform entry, whose RFC 7638 thumbprint is the one sealed here; with it the agent signature re-verifies offline.

The sealed agent_signature has one bit flipped and the envelope is re-signed with the vault key, so the chain, the envelope signature and the payload binding all hold. With the cert key supplied, the agent signature fails to verify over the sealed content_hash.

The on_behalf_of copy in entry 1 payload names a different cert thumbprint than the one sealed beside the agent signature. The copy a reader sees must equal the signed predicate.on_behalf_of, so this fails with or without agent keys.
The same fixture with no agent keys: the agent-signature check is opt-in and reports skipped_no_input, so the verdict rests on the envelope alone and passes. The vector above is what the check adds.

POST /v1/records by a cert holder with an AGLedger-On-Behalf-Of token whose act.sub is the cert identity. predicate.on_behalf_of seals the delegated subject, the act chain, validated: true and binding: bound, with the caller cert beside them.
The on_behalf_of copy in entry 1 payload rewritten from binding: bound to unbound. The copy a reader sees must equal the signed predicate.on_behalf_of.

Engine booted without a signing key: every row has signing_key_id=NULL and an all-zero signature slot. Chain integrity holds via hash links; the signature check is skipped (no key), never folded into a cryptographically-signed verdict.

Clean 3-entry chain signed under ES256 (COSE -7, P1363 low-S) by an engine booted with a P-256 vault key behind AGLEDGER_ALLOW_NON_DEFAULT_SIGNING_ALG. Requires an ES256-capable verifier (wave 2); earlier verifiers fail it CHAIN_UNSUPPORTED_ALGORITHM, fail-closed.
ES256 entry 2 signature byte flipped; the envelope still decodes and the chain claim matches, so ES256 signature verification is what fails.

ES256 entry 2 carries a cryptographically valid ES256 signature under a protected header claiming EdDSA (-8). The header alg must be asserted EQUAL to the resolved key algorithm, never used for dispatch and never softened to an upgrade notice.
